title: Finding IDs collide for identical comment bodies; baseline then hides surviving duplicates
description:
ID = <path>::<symbol-path>::<FNV1a(content)>. Two identical prose comments in the same file+symbol produce the same ID.

Repro: fn a() {}\n// same text\nfn b() {}\n// same text\n -> both findings id=a.rs::-::406c896fa7840b52. After --adopt the baseline holds one ID; deleting either comment leaves the other permanently suppressed (check passes, rc=0).

Observed in sad itself: at HEAD (baseline removed) sad/tests/extract_test.rs yields 297 findings but 296 unique IDs (2x sad/tests/extract_test.rs::-::a4c45a2a42fc754b), which is why sad-baseline.json (296 ids) reports findings_suppressed=297.

Impact: baseline suppression is not a bijection over findings; a surviving violation silently passes. Also breaks any consumer assuming unique IDs.

Expected: id includes a deterministic occurrence discriminator (e.g. occurrence index of that body within path+symbol) so ids are unique per finding while staying line-independent.
acceptance_criteria: RED: a file with two identical prose comments yields two distinct ids and a test asserts uniqueness over a fixture tree; GREEN: baseline adoption can express both, deleting one leaves the other reported, sad-baseline.json is regenerated under the new ID scheme in the same change, and just ci is green.
notes:
Review note (Rule of 5): the ID change invalidates all 296 ids in sad-baseline.json, and the shrink-only guard in check.rs refuses --adopt when ids look new. The ticket is not implementable without a baseline migration path (schema_version bump plus a deliberate re-adopt affordance, or a one-time flag). Spec also never states ID uniqueness (grep of openspec/specs/comment-gate/spec.md shows only stability wording), so the requirement must be added before the code lands.
Co-modification note: sad/src/check.rs is targeted by sad-04v, sad-kte, sad-o40 and sad-8ah. sad-04v and sad-kte are independent code paths in the same file; sequence them.
Spec note: this ticket changes openspec/specs/comment-gate/spec.md. Seven open tickets carry spec deltas; per repo policy each deployed-spec edit goes through a new openspec change, so either bundle the deltas into one change before implementation or accept seven sequential change/approve cycles.
Done in openspec change gate-field-hardening (archived as 2026-11-18-gate-field-hardening). IDs keep the bare base identity for the first occurrence and append #<n> for later identical identities in report order, applied once after all checks (cross-check collisions included). Baseline schema_version 2: v1 still suppresses exact matches; the adoption that rewrites a v1 document may add ids once, then shrink-only is restored. sad-baseline.json regenerated: 297 unique ids (+1: sad/tests/extract_test.rs::-::a4c45a2a42fc754b#2); sad check --all: 0 findings, 297 suppressed. Amended acceptance: 'deleting one of two identical comments leaves the other reported' is not achievable with a line-independent id (the survivor's identity is indistinguishable from the deleted occurrence); the restored bijection is between baseline entries and findings at adoption time, and grandfathered duplicates behave like any two grandfathered findings when one is fixed. Spec now states this explicitly.
close_reason: Unique finding ids (#n occurrence suffix) + baseline schema v2 with one-time v1 migration; baseline regenerated (297 ids)

title: Gate flags Python shebang and PEP 263 coding cookie as prose
description:
Field test across the charly-vibes fleet: 235 comment_outside_channel findings on 204 files are shebang (#!/usr/bin/env python3) or coding-cookie (-*- coding: utf-8 -*-) lines. tree-sitter-python yields these as line_comment nodes; classify() routes them to Prose because the Python header channel is the module docstring only, so no channel accepts them.

Repro (corpus /tmp/sad-edge/lang/py_traps.py):
  #!/usr/bin/env python
  # -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
sad check --all -> 2 comment_outside_channel findings on lines 1-2.

Impact: every executable Python script in every adopting repo fails the gate for mandatory file metadata. This is the single largest false-positive class found.

Expected: shebang and PEP 263 coding cookie recognized as file-metadata exemptions (exempt-but-observable, counted like SPDX), or excluded before attribution. Needs a spec change in openspec/specs/comment-gate/spec.md if the channel model is unimplementable here.
acceptance_criteria: RED: a Python file whose first line is a shebang and whose first two lines carry a PEP 263 coding cookie produces no comment_outside_channel findings, and a shebang on a later line still does; GREEN: the two lines are attributed to a documented class and remain visible in stats (exempt-but-observable, like SPDX), the spec change is merged through a new openspec change, and just ci is green.
notes: Spec note: this ticket changes openspec/specs/comment-gate/spec.md. Seven open tickets carry spec deltas; per repo policy each deployed-spec edit goes through a new openspec change, so either bundle the deltas into one change before implementation or accept seven sequential change/approve cycles.
close_reason: Python shebang (line 1) and PEP 263 coding cookie (lines 1-2) are exemption-class, counted, never prose; later-line shebang stays prose. Change 2026-11-18-python-file-metadata archived, 144 contract tests pass, just ci green.

title: Dogfood: wire sad gate into sad repo lefthook pre-commit/pre-push
description:
## Objective
Run `sad hooks install` in this repository so `sad check` gates
pre-commit AND pre-push as a sad-managed block, alongside (not inside)
the ddl-managed blocks. This is the actual gate the tool has lacked.

## Test shape (red first)
Red proof first: `lefthook run pre-commit` / `pre-push` currently does
NOT run sad. Land order: install, verify both blocks present (managed_block
reader or lefthook dry-run), then negative test: a seeded comment violation
makes the hook exit nonzero.

## Acceptance
- lefthook.yml diff committed showing both stages wired; ddl-managed
  blocks byte-identical before/after.
- `lefthook run pre-commit` and `pre-push` pass on clean HEAD; the
  pre-existing self-gate warning severity knob decided in sad-t7y must
  not block the hook when it is non-error severity.
- `just ci` green after wiring.
- .beads/issues.jsonl exported and committed per tracked-export invariant.

## Anti-goals
- No edits to ddl-managed blocks.
- No --no-verify workflow changes; no CI workflow edits.

title: Honor .gitignore during source discovery (sad-8ah decision a)
description:
Decision (sad-8ah option a): discovery honors `.gitignore` files inside a git work tree by parsing them directly — no git binary, no index, no user/global config, no `.git/info/exclude`, no network. Full design: `.wai/projects/sad/designs/2026-11-18-gitignore-and-generated-path-off-ramp.md`.

## Field evidence

sad-8ah records 52 gitignored sources outside discovery's fixed 14-name skip list across the fleet: tambor 33 generated `.ts` under `src/docs/content/generated/`, incitaciones 16 vendored agent-skill scripts under `.agents|.claude/skills/*/scripts/`, miblioteca 2, wanna 1. Both dominant classes are already declared ignored by the repositories themselves, so honoring ignore files fixes them with zero per-repo `sad.toml` configuration, while generated files mostly lack the `@generated` marker.

## Chosen semantics

- Applies only when `<repo>/.git` exists (directory, or file for linked worktrees/submodules); the `.git` contents are never read. Otherwise discovery is byte-for-byte the pre-change walk. No upward search from the given repo root.
- Root and nested `.gitignore` files only, evaluated for entries the walk reaches; a deeper file's rules override a shallower file's rules, and the last matching rule in a file wins.
- `#` comment and blank lines skipped; `!` negation supported.
- A trailing `/` makes the rule directory-only; an ignored directory is pruned, so a negation cannot re-include a path below an ignored directory (mirrors git).
- A slash-less pattern matches a basename at any depth (compiled as `**/name`); a pattern with a leading or embedded `/` is anchored at the ignore file's directory.
- `*` and `?` match within one path segment and never cross `/`; `**` segments span zero or more segments; character classes, brace expansion, and backslash escapes are not interpreted (literal), mirroring `exemptions::glob_match`'s closed grammar.
- A missing, unreadable, or non-UTF-8 `.gitignore` contributes no rules; an unreadable root file falls back to the current walk. Discovery cannot hard-fail on ignore parsing.
- Tracked status is not consulted: a tracked file matching an ignore pattern is skipped (documented divergence from `git status`).
- No new envelope counter: ignored paths are invisible exactly like `SKIPPED_DIRECTORIES`, so no `files_ignored` stat and no new warning channel in this change.
- The implementation lives in `sad/src/check/discovery.rs`; `sad/src/exemptions.rs` is not modified (that matcher is root-anchored `sad.toml` exclude globbing, a different contract).

## Determinism caveat

The result stays a pure function of tree bytes plus repo-relative path — no clock, network, git invocation, index, `$HOME`, global excludes, or environment — but ignore files are part of the tree, so the same source bytes can be gated in one checkout and skipped in another after a branch switch or `git clean` changes `.gitignore` content. The spec delta must state this contract: ignored sources are out of scope, and re-inclusion is done by editing `.gitignore` (or moving the file), never by `sad.toml`.

## Target files

- `sad/src/check/discovery.rs` — parse root/nested `.gitignore`, evaluate rules during the walk, prune ignored directories.
- `sad/tests/check_discovery_gitignore_test.rs` (new) — red-phase fixture tests.
- `openspec/specs/comment-gate/spec.md` — through a new `openspec/changes/<slug>/` delta only, never a direct deployed-spec edit.

## Named failing tests (red phase, a targeted run must find each)

- `gitignored_sources_are_not_gated` — a git work tree (`.git/` present) containing a gitignored generated source with findings-eligible prose yields no findings for that path, and discovery's file list omits it.
- `not_gated_source_in_non_ignored_path_stays_gated` — a source in a path that merely looks generated/vendored but matches no ignore rule stays gated; proves discovery keys on ignore content, not path-name heuristics.

## Acceptance

`cargo test --package sad --test check_discovery_gitignore_test` passes with both named tests; existing discovery unit tests (trees without `.git`) still pass unchanged, proving the non-git fallback; no new envelope fields; spec delta validated with `openspec validate <change> --strict` before implementation lands.
close_reason: Discovery honors .gitignore inside a git work tree: .git trigger, root+nested files, deeper override with last-match, closed grammar (basename-any-depth, / anchoring, trailing /, !, *, ?, ** segments, literal classes/braces, CRLF trim), total fallbacks, tracked status not consulted, no new counter/warning. Change 2026-11-18-gitignore-aware-discovery archived; 150 contract tests pass; just ci green; self-gate 0 blocking/1 warning.

title: Raise commented_out_code precision before restoring error severity
description: The field investigation found 14/14 commented_out_code findings on 48 repos were banners, math formulas, or expected-value annotations — zero dead code. Narrow the predicate (exclude formula/annotation/separator shapes, require a code-shaped parse with declarations/statements) and add a precision corpus; then promote the finding back to error severity in a spec change.
close_reason: Predicate narrowed: no-alnum bodies rejected, root must carry a declaration/control statement, bare call/assignment/new-expression/formula/annotation roots stay prose; corpus pinned. commented_out_code restored to error severity; banner reclassification stays warning. Change archived, 144 contract tests pass.

title: Triage comment smells by severity instead of flagging all prose
description: Turn comment findings into quality triage: name the smell (narration/apology/todo/banner/dead code/doc cap/unclassified), block only on high-confidence errors, treat rationale tags (SAFETY/INVARIANT/SECURITY) as a channel, count doc caps in sentences, and enforce on the baseline delta. Supersedes the blanket comment_outside_channel verdict. OpenSpec change: comment-smell-triage, with the field-investigation evidence (58,781 findings: 42.5% tests, 24.7% noise, 0.08% TODO/apology).
notes: Rule-of-5 review applied: severity now covers every finding kind (smell null for structural checks); commented_out_code ships warning-only until sad-jdw restores precision/error; --strict added for fail-on-warnings; narration/apology/doc-cap algorithms pinned; shared post-check classifier; rationale tags include WHY (NOTE stays prose); suppression never withholds errors; evidence.md records the corpus.

title: No gitignore or generated-path off-ramp: gitignored sources are gated
description:
Discovery ignores .gitignore by design (untracked files are in scope) and recognizes only a fixed 14-name skip list plus a leading @generated marker. Two real classes therefore gate by default:

- generated-but-gitignored sources: tambor src/docs/content/generated/*.ts (33 files)
- vendored tooling: incitaciones .agents|.claude/skills/*/scripts/*.py

Fleet count of gitignored sources outside the skip list: 52 (tambor 33, incitaciones 16, miblioteca 2, wanna 1).

Excludes are per-repo sad.toml globs, so every adopter must hand-write them, and no init command seeds a config. Generated files also lack the @generated marker in most codegen outputs.

Expected: decide between (a) honoring .gitignore when inside a git work tree (documented determinism caveat), (b) path heuristics for generated/vendor trees, or (c) an init subcommand that writes sad.toml with detected excludes. Whichever lands, spec + docs must state the contract.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded (design note or spec change) choosing between gitignore awareness, generated/vendor path heuristics, and an init subcommand that seeds sad.toml excludes; the chosen option gets a follow-up implementation ticket with a named failing test and a documented determinism caveat.
notes:
Co-modification note: sad/src/check/discovery.rs is targeted by sad-54i, sad-xkz, sad-o40, sad-7hx and sad-8ah. Land discovery changes sequentially (sad-54i and sad-xkz are S; both after sad-o40 settles the reporting channel).
Spec note: this ticket changes openspec/specs/comment-gate/spec.md. Seven open tickets carry spec deltas; per repo policy each deployed-spec edit goes through a new openspec change, so either bundle the deltas into one change before implementation or accept seven sequential change/approve cycles.
close_reason: Decision recorded (option a: honor .gitignore in a git work tree by parsing ignore files; no git binary, no user/global config) in .wai/projects/sad/designs/2026-11-18-gitignore-and-generated-path-off-ramp.md. Follow-up implementation ticket sad-z6q filed with named failing tests and determinism caveat.

title: @ts-expect-error is not a recognized suppression form (only deprecated @ts-ignore)
description:
attribution::parse_directive recognizes noqa, 'type: ignore', '@ts-ignore', 'eslint-disable', 'sad:ignore'. TypeScript's current recommended directive is @ts-expect-error; it falls through to Prose.

Fleet evidence: ~80 comment_outside_channel findings whose text begins with '@ts-expect-error' (e.g. 'node builtin ...'), all classified as prose instead of suppression debt.

Impact: adopting repos cannot record the directive their compiler requires without it counting as a documentation violation, and the spec's closed list (openspec/specs/comment-gate/spec.md 'Suppression debt is exempt-but-counted') enshrines the deprecated form.

Expected: add '@ts-expect-error' alongside '@ts-ignore' (spec + attribution + tests).
acceptance_criteria: RED: a comment starting with @ts-expect-error is classified as suppression, not prose, and the fleet clip is re-run to confirm the ~80 findings disappear from comment_outside_channel and appear in suppression_debt; GREEN: spec directive list updated through a new openspec change and just ci is green.
notes: Spec note: this ticket changes openspec/specs/comment-gate/spec.md. Seven open tickets carry spec deltas; per repo policy each deployed-spec edit goes through a new openspec change, so either bundle the deltas into one change before implementation or accept seven sequential change/approve cycles.
close_reason: @ts-expect-error recognized as unscoped suppression (ts_expect_error), counted as suppression_debt. Change 2026-11-18-ts-expect-error-suppression archived, just ci green.

title: Gate ignores .js and .mjs sources silently
description:
SOURCE_EXTENSIONS is exactly [rs, py, ts] (sad/src/check/discovery.rs). Fleet inventory of ungated sources (excluding target/node_modules/.venv/dist/build): .js 843, .mjs 64; .tsx/.mts/.cts/.jsx are 0 in the fleet today but common in TS projects.

Silent: no warning, no stat, no finding; the file does not exist for the gate.

Impact: a TS repo with JS build/config sources has a permanent blind spot, and the docs claim TypeScript support without naming its boundary.

Expected: add js/mjs to the TypeScript routing (tree-sitter-typescript parses JavaScript), and emit a discovery warning for adjacent unsupported extensions (.tsx/.mts/.cts/.jsx) so the boundary is visible rather than silent. Document the extension set in the spec and docs/src/gate-model.md.

Anti-goal: do not add .jsx/.tsx parsing under this ticket; JSX grammars are a separate decision.
acceptance_criteria: RED: a tree with one .js and one .mjs file containing prose comments yields findings or an explicit unsupported-extension warning; GREEN: discovery tests cover the new extensions, files_discovered reflects them, and just ci stays green; adjacent-but-unsupported extensions (.tsx/.mts/.cts/.jsx) emit a warning instead of vanishing.
notes:
Review note (Rule of 5): split out .pyi coverage into sad-7hx; the JS-family extension support is independent of stub docstring semantics. Shared file sad/src/check/discovery.rs is also targeted by sad-8ah and sad-xkz, so sequence those three or expect overlapping edits.

title: commented_out_code parses unbounded prose runs: superlinear cliff
description:
blocks() groups a maximal adjacent prose run into one body and commented_out_code parses that whole body with tree-sitter. On long runs of plain prose (no valid code) the grammar's error recovery dominates and cost grows ~quadratically.

Measured (single file, all lines '// line N', release binary, --all --json):
  1000 -> 54ms, 2000 -> 157ms, 4000 -> 496ms, 8000 -> 1796ms, 16000 -> 10008ms, 32000 -> 63343ms, 200000 -> >90s (timeout)
Same 16000 comments split over 16 files -> 1179ms (so the cost is intra-file/intra-run).
Attribution: 16000 lines 8715ms default vs 1457ms with checks.commented_out_code=false.

Also note the run body has no size cap, so memory scales with the run.

Expected: bound the predicate input (node count or byte cap per run, chunk long runs) and/or cheap pre-filter (body must contain code-ish tokens) before parsing; add a regression test at 8k/32k lines asserting a time or work bound.
acceptance_criteria: RED: a regression test with a 32k-line contiguous prose run completes under the agreed bound (measured baseline today: 63s) and still reports the same findings as a shorter run; GREEN: no finding changes for runs below the cap, the cap is documented in the spec/doc comment, and just ci is green.
notes:
Review note (Rule of 5): state the bound numerically (e.g. 32k-line run under 2s) and add the anti-goal: capping must not change findings for runs below the cap, or the cap becomes a way to hide commented-out code. Located at blocks()/parses_as_code in sad/src/checks/commented_out_code.rs.
Done in gate-field-hardening. MAX_PREDICATE_BYTES=8192 / MAX_PREDICATE_LINES=512 in commented_out_code; bodies within both bounds parse as one unit (unchanged findings), longer runs are chunked at line boundaries and match when any chunk matches; whole body still hashes into the finding id. Fail-closed on a chunk-boundary split and on a single line over the byte bound. Regression: 32k manually built prose nodes complete in ~4.4s debug under the 20s bound and keep 32k per-node findings; a dead-code item wholly inside a chunk past the bound still yields one block finding.
close_reason: Bounded chunked predicate (8192 bytes / 512 lines) with 32k-line regression

title: Default scope selects 0 files and reports pass with no signal
description:
Behavior is spec-conforming (openspec/specs/comment-gate/spec.md, Requirement: Agent-attribution scoping; sad/src/scope.rs rationale: working-tree state is never treated as evidence). The defect is observability, not selection.

Repro (git repo, tracked file edited, nothing else):
  printf "fn a() {}\n// ONLY unstaged modification\n" > src/a.rs
  sad check  -> files_selected=0, "pass: 0 findings in 0 files", rc=0

Also observed: a staged-but-uncommitted file and an untracked file ARE selected (no governing commit), so the local loop silently skips exactly the legacy file the agent just edited.

Impact: an agent editing an existing file gets a green gate that gated nothing; nothing in the output distinguishes this from a genuine clean run.

Expected: surface the scope decision. Emit selected/attributed/skipped-by-attribution counts in the text render and envelope (reuse the stats coverage pattern from sad-o40), and state the widening path (--all, or commit with the configured trailer) in the message. Keep selection semantics exactly as the spec requires.

Anti-goal: do NOT add working-tree state (unstaged/staged/untracked diff) to attribution evidence; that contradicts the ratified scoping requirement and scope.rs policy.
acceptance_criteria: RED: a zero-selection run is distinguishable from a clean run in both text and envelope; GREEN: counts for selected/attributed/skipped and the widening hint are asserted in scope_test and check_envelope_test, and just ci is green.
notes:
Co-modification note: sad/src/check.rs is targeted by sad-04v, sad-kte, sad-o40 and sad-8ah. sad-04v and sad-kte are independent code paths in the same file; sequence them.
Done in gate-field-hardening. scope::select_in_scope reports ScopeSelection{files, attributed, without_commit, unattributed}; stats gain files_attributed, files_without_commit, files_unattributed; text mode appends the attribution decision plus the widening paths (--all, or commit with the configured trailer) when a default run selected nothing but candidates existed. Selection semantics unchanged (no working-tree evidence). Tests: scope_test::selection_reports_what_attribution_scope_did, check_stats_test::scope_counts_explain_a_zero_selection_run, check_envelope_test::text_mode_names_the_attribution_scope_when_nothing_is_selected.
close_reason: Scope counters in stats + one-line attribution hint; selection semantics unchanged

title: Decide .pyi stub coverage for the doc channel
description:
Fleet inventory: 12 .pyi files, all currently invisible to the gate (SOURCE_EXTENSIONS = rs|py|ts).

Why it matters rather than being a plain extension gap: .pyi stubs are where a Python package states its public API, and the channel model says public-API doc-comments are the one legitimate prose channel. Leaving stubs ungated means the documented-prose surface most likely to hold prose is the surface the gate cannot see.

Decision needed: analyze stubs as Python (tree-sitter-python handles .pyi), analyze them with docstring rules only, or exclude them explicitly with a documented reason. Choose before implementing extension support so discovery and the spec change land together.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded (design note or spec change) stating whether .pyi stubs are analyzed, and if analyzed, how docstrings in stubs map to the doc channel; follow-up implementation ticket filed with a failing test named.
